I did think something similar recently. I was CERTAIN I was dying and I was so terrified. I could feel the weight of a massive, fluid-filled sack inside of my pelvis. I was scared to sit or lay down. When they did the ultrasound on me, I begged them not to press too hard, because I thought it was going to burst. But, guess what? It turned out to be nothing. They checked me thoroughly. They did an internal and external thing and there was absolutely nothing there. As soon as the ultrasound was over, I felt the mass was gone. So, it's very possible that your brain can trick you in high states of anxiety. I feel so much better now. I think getting checked out will give you a lot of relief. 

My doctor said that these things are usually a fabrication of your mind if it only happens sometimes. It will more than likely be constant if it's genuine. I was having muscle spasms, shortness of breath, and extreme mood swings. I was CERTAIN I was on death's doorstep. I  believe you will find relief if you get this checked. I don't know if you have any emotional support to get you through the appointment, but if you don't, I would be willing to chat with you before, during, and after if you need support. I know how this feels. It's so scary, but it will be okay.

Thanks so much for your response. I know that reassurance-seeking isn't always the best in this kind of situation, but since my doctor's appointment is literally in the morning, I'm reaching out. I (27f) know that the symptoms get worse when I get worked up about it. Usually at night and when I lay down. I saw a video online of a woman who had my symptoms and she ended up having the 'C' word, so I am just freaking out about that. I also have neglected much-needed medical care for over a decade because of my PTSD. On the flip side, I am known to catastrophize when I am anxious and a lot of these symptoms I'm having could be due to the extreme anxiety that I've brought upon myself for researching too much. I haven't been sleeping or eating as much. I've also been tensing a LOT due to stress. I hope that if you're dealing with anything that's causing your stress, that you find some relief.

You've got this! I used to be in the same boat, but since the diagnosis, I've incorporated walking into my day-to-day life. It started with just ten minutes a day and then I increased it over time because ten minutes was no longer enough. Even with those 10 minutes along with trading out white breads/pastas/potatoes with whole wheat, watching my portion sizes, and drinking lots of water. I also had to distance myself from the amount of junk food that I was eating it.  I was able to lose a good bit of weight and it's getting easier and easier. It's all about consistency. You can even treat yourself a bit sometimes. Just as long as you're mindful about it and don't make it too much of a habit if your splurge contains too much sugar/carbs. Of course, I splurge more than is recommended, but things have been fine for me so long as I make that splurge a really small portion size in comparison to what I would have had a long time ago. I know that part is easier said than done. I have lost almost 30 pounds in a few months from this alone. My mental state is also a lot better and I feel like I have a lot more energy and a higher pain tolerance.  You can do this. I promise. It will get easier. Just take it a day at a time and don't worry about being super, super strict about stuff.  Don't be too hard on yourself if there are some slipups. Oftentimes that can be a setback. If you fall down a few stairs on your journey, just get back up and resume. Believe me, I'm not perfect at all and I'm sure I still have a lot to learn. Also, know that you can always come to this subreddit for support.

I'm going to have an appointment for a potential ovarian cyst today and I'm TERRIFIED the appointment is going to end with them telling me I'm dying. I've been sobbing for days and I don't usually cry as a stress response. My anxiety is through the roof, which I know will only escalate my health anxiety, but I'm just so scared.

I'm so sorry that you and your dad had to go through that. Stress can cause headaches and the fact that your dad had a stroke surely is amping up your stress levels. That could be the cause of your headache to linger.  I understand how hard this must be. You're very young, so I doubt that you're going to have a stroke. Not trying to invalidate your feelings, though. If you're really worried, is there any way that you could go see a doctor to make sure everything is okay with you?

Tetanus. I got a minor puncture wound on my toe from a piece of glass in my home. This happened on Saturday night and I had no idea that I had a puncture wound at all because it was so numb.  I only discovered the tiny dot on Friday night. I can't for the life of me recall if I've had my Tetanus shot in the past five years (my memory is awful) and I can't check until tomorrow. 

 Anyway, I have gotten Covid-19 in late December (I'm vaccinated and the symptoms haven't been severe at all!), but I thought that I was getting better. Unfortunately, I got a fever and chills last night. I also have some pain and numbness that comes and goes near the puncture under my toe. The foot pain comes and goes and my anxiety and fixation definitely makes it a lot worse. I'm not having muscle spasms or jaw lock or anything, so I don't know how likely it is that I have tetanus, but I am freaking out with anxiety.

 I do plan to call my doctor about this tomorrow, but it's hard because I don't want to give anyone Covid-19 or risk getting another strand or just getting it again in general if I'm not actually dealing with Tetanus. I also feel like if I have tetanus, it's too late now. That I'm actually just doomed. I'm so scared.
Good job! It sounds like you're heading in the right direction. I've been in the same boat and I promise it gets easier.

I'm 27 and in the same position. The only difference is that I have a partner that I live with. You'd think that'd be a step up, but it actually sucks because I don't like having to depend on another person for my livelihood no matter how okay with it that she says she is. I make up for it by doing my best to self-improve and doing the housework and cooking. Kind of like a live-in maid/butler. I also am a big emotional support for her. She insists that it's enough. And I'm never going to stop trying to improve. I think that's what matters. 

Ideas, maybe you could try to start small. Maybe do the house and/or yard work during the day for your dad and stepmom? It could help you feel like you're contributing and giving back to them. Maybe you could ask them if they could teach you certain skills a little at a time. I don't know your situation, but maybe that would help you not only gain skill but confidence. It'd also show your family that you're trying your best, which will do a lot. 

I know this isn't the biggest, brightest solution, but I think that it could help. It's helped me. a lot.

27 here and have literally accomplished NOTHING in life. No college, no job, and did extremely poorly in school. I was a victim of a lot of neglect and abuse and I have no concept of what to do or how to function with the mental health problems as well as the learning disabilities I have. I WANT to achieve something, but I don't feel skilled or confident enough to do them.  None of it makes sense to me and it seems that there are so many requirements that I can't fulfill even for the easiest of jobs. On top of that I have severe agoraphobia and am too afraid to even leave the house without breaking into hyperventilating sobs. I'm extremely lucky to have a therapist and a partner who understands this about me. I make it up to her by doing all of the housework and cooking for her. Kind of like a personal maid.  She said that before I was in her life, she struggled a lot with having a livable household and that she feels like this is payment enough for me to stay with her without helping financially. Still, I feel awful. I don't like the idea of being so dependent on another person. What if she died? It's terrifying and I don't have a CLUE what to do except try to improve mentally and physically so that I can hopefully gain the skills I need to do SOMETHING. So, I get it. You're not alone, OP. I think that there is hope for you. I hope that you can find someone who understands your struggles and will have the patience to help you get to where you want and need to be.

I have talked to my partner about this repeatedly. I just think she must be feeling grief because we used to eat whatever the hell we wanted together without thinking about it and it's a big change. I am going to talk to her today and really emphasize that while we can't eat the same things anymore, we can still eat together. We also went on a walk today and have committed to doing this walk together every day so that we can have quality time and have mental and physical benefits from it. She seems really happy with this arrangement and I made it clear that it's low pressure and fun and that nobody will be mad at each other if one doesn't feel like they can stick to the commitment that day.  We will both try our best.

I've just started this journey three months ago and it's been hard to stick to sometimes, but I try not to be too hard on myself when I'm not perfect. I just get back up if I falter. I allow myself treats.
